historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR 9.6% vs revenue 3yr CAGR 48.8% -- divergence far above 30%. Equity growth is suppressed by $1.5B+ of buybacks and equity-award tax payments since 2023; revenue growth is flattered by recovery from the FY2022 trough (FY2022 revenue $1,358M was itself down 25% on the meme-era FY2021). Neither is a clean forward rate; the base path (avg ~8%/yr) sits near the equity figure, deliberately.
historical_growth.notes: EPS CAGRs undefined (negative EPS in FY2020-FY2023 start points: FY2022 -1.17, FY2020 +0.01 off a near-zero base). Equity 5yr undefined (negative FY2020 equity, pre-IPO preferred structure). FCF CAGRs NOT computed: reported FCF is customer-fund flows (FY2021 -$948M, FY2022 -$880M, FY2023 +$1,181M OCF, FY2024 -$157M OCF), so neither a reported nor an SBC-adjusted series carries information. SBC plus equity-award taxes was $1,994M in FY2021, $666M FY2022, $883M FY2023, $548M FY2024, $742M FY2025 and ~$415M FY2026E -- falling as a share of revenue from >100% to ~8%.

scenario_narratives.base: Robinhood keeps compounding customer assets (Total Platform Assets $396B, +19% YoY) but at a decelerating pace (net deposits 17% annualised in Q3-2026 vs 29% a year earlier), and revenue grows slower than assets because the two cyclical engines cool together: Fed cuts take the high-margin net interest line down first (FY2027 +8% only), and options/equities activity normalises from record margin balances. Event contracts survive in most states but Robinhood's routed-volume share keeps eroding to exchange-owned apps; crypto is a modest, volatile line rather than a recovery. Gold, banking, card and TradePMR advisory carry the mid-decade growth at ~10-11%, EBITDA margin settles ~51% with SBC drifting to 6%. Owner FCF ~$1.8B FY2026E growing to ~$3.4B by FY2036.
scenario_narratives.bull: Prediction markets become a durable, large category: the CFTC-preemption argument wins at the circuit/Supreme Court level, Rothera E&C's own exchange and clearing restores economics lost to Kalshi routing, and sports/election/economic contracts become a second options-sized franchise. A renewed retail and crypto cycle lifts transaction revenue, Gold crosses ~10M subscribers, banking and the Gold Card scale profitably, and international (UK, EU, Canada via WonderFi, Indonesia/Singapore) adds a second leg. Revenue roughly triples over the decade, operating leverage takes EBITDA margin to 56% (the IBKR-direction outcome of a vertically integrated, self-clearing platform), and SBC falls to 5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2022 template, with a legal overlay. Retail trading cools after a high-market peak (options and margin interest fall together as margin balances deleverage), crypto stays in its slump, the Fed cuts compress net interest, and adverse rulings in the multi-state event-contract litigation force sports contracts out of key states -- removing most of the ~12% of revenue that event contracts now represent. Revenue falls ~12% in FY2027 and then grows only 2-6% a year as Robinhood competes on price for a maturing customer base (net deposits already decelerating); PFOF/best-execution rule changes are a further tail. EBITDA margin compresses to 40% and recovers only to 44% as the cost base (international, Rothera, AI) proves sticky; SBC stays near 7-9%.
scenario_narratives.valuation_finding: On every scenario -- including the street (SBC-as-non-cash) basis of the bull case -- value sits below the price, so band_position lands far above 100%: the price is outside the accounting-regime band, not inside it. Today's EV is ~40x FY2026E owner FCF against a 13.7x implied base exit multiple; the market is capitalising sustained high growth at a sub-10% discount rate. The model's view is that $81 capitalises FY2023-26 growth that rests on cyclical activity, rates and a one-year-old, litigated product line.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on a normalised, revenue-built cash flow -- reported OCF is customer-fund noise for a self-clearing broker. SBC (including equity-award taxes) fully expensed and the share count held flat; operating net interest on customer balances kept in the flows, corporate-cash interest stripped and corporate cash added net of the convertible and a liquidity reserve. The base deliberately does not extrapolate the FY2023-26 revenue CAGR: FY2026 earnings rest on high market levels, record margin balances, pre-cut interest rates and a new litigated product line, while crypto has already rolled over. Cyclicality is charged once, through a 30% bear weight and a 15x terminal cap, not by stacking a premium on the WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Event-contract litigation: adverse circuit/Supreme Court rulings on CFTC preemption could remove most of ~12% of revenue; a favourable ruling is the main bull lever
Retail trading cyclicality: options, equities and crypto transaction revenue (60% of total) can fall 25%+ in a risk-off year (FY2022 precedent)
Rate path: Fed cuts hit net interest revenue (31% of total) at near-100% incremental margin
PFOF / best-execution regulation: a ban or restructuring would reset transaction economics
Share loss in prediction markets and crypto to exchange-owned venues (Kalshi, Coinbase, Crypto.com)
Terminal value is 54% of base EV; each 1pp on the discount rate moves base value ~8% (required-return table: $45.16 at 9%, $32.78 at 12%)
Operating-liquidity reserve ($1.0B) is a judgment; a clearinghouse deposit spike can consume more

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular-session close); 52-week range 63.52-139.75
data_sources.financials: HOOD_Metrics.csv (SEC XBRL, FY2019-FY2025 and quarters to Q3-2026); 10-Q Q3-2026 (balance sheet, statements of operations and cash flows, Note 6 revenue disaggregation, Note 11 convertible notes, EPS note); 10-K FY2025 (corporate-cash interest history, leases, NCI)
data_sources.qualitative: HOOD_Analysis.json (2026-11-08): revenue mix, Q3-2026 guidance (adjusted opex + SBC $2.675-2.75B), event-contract litigation, net deposit deceleration, M&A

inputs.sbc_source: 10-Q Q3-2026 cash flow statement: share-based compensation $277M for 9M-2026 (annualised ~$370M) plus taxes paid on net share settlement of equity awards $34M 9M (~$45M FY). No combined adjusted-EBITDA SBC line in the 10-Q, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 comparators: SBC $305M + equity-award taxes $437M (the 2024-25 taxes were inflated by founder/IPO-era award vesting).
inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 diluted weighted average 911M (basic 898M + 13M dilutive options/RSUs, treasury method). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. The $2.2B 0% 2029 convertible (conversion price ~$174, 5.7332 sh per $1,000) is out of the money at the current price and is treated as debt, not shares; capped calls ignored.
inputs.fy0_build: FY2026E total net revenue = 9M actual $3,799M + Q4E $1,400M (Q3 $1,424M; Q4-2025 $1,283M; event contracts accelerating against rate-cut pressure on net interest and weak crypto) = ~$5,199M. Less interest on corporate cash and investments (9M $112M + Q4E $45M = $157M), which is stripped because the corporate cash is added in the bridge = base_revenue $5,042M. FY2026E costs: guided adjusted opex + SBC $2.675-2.75B (Q3-2026 call, narrowed) plus provision for credit losses ~$230M. Implied EBITDA before SBC ~51% of ex-interest revenue; D&A ~$97M (1.9%); capex (PP&E + capitalised software) ~$85M (1.7%).
inputs.reported_fcf_note: Reported OCF/FCF is meaningless for a self-clearing broker: it is dominated by customer-fund and stock-loan flows (FY2024 OCF -$157M, FY2025 +$1,638M, 9M-2026 +$3,983M against 9M net income $1,395M). reported_fcf here is therefore a NORMALISED pre-SBC figure (owner FCF + SBC incl. equity-award taxes + corporate-cash interest) so that last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc_incl_equity_taxes - interest_income holds; last_fcf is the FY2026E component-built owner FCF (EBITDA 51% - SBC 8.2% - D&A 1.9% at ~15% cash tax, + D&A - capex).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10-yr UST ~4.3% + ERP 5.0% x beta ~1.25 (blended: raw HOOD beta is >2, but the business is now profitable, net-cash and diversified across options/NII/subscriptions; a raw-beta CAPM of ~14-15% would double-charge the cyclicality that the 30% bear weight already carries) = ~10.5%. Capital structure is effectively all-equity (0% convert, net cash), so WACC ~ cost of equity. Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is charged through the scenario weights, not the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Leases immaterial (total lease liabilities $221M FY2025 against ~$5B revenue); lease cost left inside the EBITDA margin, lease liabilities NOT in net debt. One treatment.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is small (book $77M at 2026-09-30; $16M of 9M-2026 net income, mostly the Rothera JV). Flows are consolidated; the NCI is deducted once at book in the equity bridge.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Corporate cash and equivalents $5,829M (2026-09-30) less the $2,200M principal of the 0% convertible notes due 2029 = net cash $3,629M. EXCLUDED from debt: Credit Card Funding Trust asset-backed notes (~$490M of the $2,660M long-term borrowings) and drawn/undrawn broker credit facilities, because they fund operating assets (card receivables, margin/clearing) whose interest spread is inside revenue. EXCLUDED from cash: segregated customer cash ($13.4B), receivables from users, securities borrowed, clearing deposits -- all customer/operating balances matched by payables to users and securities loaned. Corporate-cash interest ($157M FY2026E) is stripped from base_revenue so the cash is not counted twice.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (operating-company row of dcf-methods routing), adapted for a self-clearing retail broker. Considered and rejected residual income on tangible book (bank row): Robinhood is not a deposit taker funding a loan book with leverage -- customer cash is segregated or swept to partner banks, and the economics are a fee/spread platform with ~51% EBITDA margins and low capital intensity, so a revenue -> margin -> owner-FCF build captures it better than ROE on book. The broker-specific adaptations are (1) build from revenue and margins, never from reported OCF (customer flows), (2) net interest revenue on margin/sweep/segregated cash/card is OPERATING revenue and stays in the flows, (3) only interest on corporate cash is stripped, matched by adding corporate cash net of the convertible, (4) a $1.0B operating-liquidity reserve is held back from the cash (clearinghouse deposit spikes forced a $3.4B emergency raise in Jan-2021; FINRA caps upstream dividends), and (5) working capital is modelled as a small NEGATIVE capture because card-receivable and margin-book growth consume regulatory capital and equity (9M-2026 card receivables grew ~$0.87B against only ~$0.23B of net CCFT funding). FIRST valuation of this ticker; no prior DCF and no MEMORY entry. Buybacks: a genuine repurchaser ($653M FY2025, $689M 9M-2026, plus $290M bought with convert proceeds) -- the flat count is being funded, so the convention matches reality. Peak-earnings check: FY2026E is not obviously a peak on every line -- crypto transaction revenue is already down ~48-55% YoY -- but options, margin interest and equities are riding high market levels and record margin balances, net interest faces rate cuts, and ~12% of revenue (event contracts) is a one-year-old, litigation-exposed line. The base case therefore does not extrapolate the FY2023-26 revenue CAGR (~41%); it compounds platform-asset growth with a deceleration.
inputs.analysis_json_fix: HOOD_Analysis.json had a missing closing brace on the event-contracts regulatory risk entry (invalid JSON); the brace was added, no content changed.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +8%: Fed cuts compress net interest (31% of revenue, already -9% YoY in Q3-2026), crypto stays subdued, event contracts keep growing but lose share to Kalshi/Coinbase/Crypto.com venues. FY2028-30 +10-11%: tracks Total Platform Assets growth (+19% YoY, net deposits decelerating 29%->17% annualised) at a lower take rate, plus Gold (+34% subs), banking, card and TradePMR advisory. Fades to 3.5% by FY2036.
base.margin_rationale: FY2026E EBITDA before SBC ~51% of ex-interest revenue. Dips to 49% in FY2027 because the lost net interest is near-100% margin and credit-card provisions are rising; recovers to 51% on operating leverage. Not taken higher: management is reinvesting (international, Rothera exchange build, AI), and mature brokers in a lower-rate world (Schwab ~45-50% pre-tax) do not sustain more.
base.sbc_rationale: 8.2% actual (SBC $370M + equity-award taxes ~$45M on ex-interest revenue) gliding ~0.4pp/yr to 6.0%.
base.tax_rationale: Cash taxes ~$300M FY2026E (9M $230M) on ~$2.1B pre-tax = ~15%: NOL and SBC deductions still sheltering. GAAP ETR 9M-2026 20%. Ramps to 24% (21% federal + state) by FY2031.
base.wc_rationale: -10% of the revenue increment: card-receivable and margin-book growth absorb equity and regulatory capital that customer payables and ABS funding do not cover.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (up from the 15% default): transaction revenue (60% of total) is retail-sentiment-driven and has already shown a 25% revenue collapse (FY2022), net interest faces explicit rate-cut guidance, and the fastest-growing line depends on an unresolved state-vs-CFTC legal question. Base 50%: the platform-asset compounding and product breadth are real and visible in Gold/AUM data. Bull 20% (down from 35%): it needs several independent things at once -- a favourable preemption ruling, regaining prediction-market share, and a renewed retail/crypto cycle.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
